about.headline: The puzzle game where every move is a decision worth making.
about.paragraph1: Coin Sort presents a set of tubes, each filled with a randomly ordered stack of differently coloured coins. You tap a tube to pick up the top coin, then tap another tube to place it — but only if the tube is empty or the top coin there matches the colour you're holding. Sort every tube to a single colour to complete the level. Early levels have three or four colours across a handful of tubes; later levels pack six colours into eight tubes with tighter empty-tube margins.
about.paragraph2: Coin Sort runs entirely in your browser. Open the Play page on any device and the puzzle loads immediately — no account, no installation, no payment. The game pauses automatically when you leave the tab and resumes exactly where you left off. Sessions can be as short as two minutes or as long as an extended puzzle session — the pacing is entirely yours.

howToPlayPage.intro: Coin Sort is a colour-sorting puzzle where you move coins between tubes to group each colour into its own stack. Every tube starts with a mixed random arrangement. Your moves are constrained: you can only pick up the top coin from any tube, and you can only place it onto an empty tube or one where the current top coin matches your colour. The challenge isn't the rule set — it's thinking far enough ahead to avoid creating configurations where no further valid moves exist.

steps.title: Identify Blocked Colours
steps.desc: Before moving anything, find which colours are most split across tubes. A colour that appears on top in several tubes simultaneously is the most accessible to consolidate. A colour buried under three other colours in every tube it appears in is the most constrained. Start by working on the accessible colours first — they create space for the harder ones.

steps.title: Use Empty Tubes Wisely
steps.desc: Empty tubes are your primary resource in Coin Sort. They function as temporary holding positions, allowing you to move coins out of the way to access coins beneath them. Don't fill empty tubes permanently with mismatched colours early in the puzzle — doing so eliminates your flexibility for later moves.

steps.title: Build Complete Stacks
steps.desc: The most efficient Coin Sort strategy is to fully complete one colour's tube before moving to the next. A completed tube (all coins of one colour, tube full) removes those coins from active consideration and reduces the complexity of the remaining puzzle. Partially sorting several colours simultaneously tends to create tangled configurations.

mechanic.title: Move Constraints and Validity
mechanic.desc: The core mechanic of Coin Sort is the move validity rule: a coin can only be placed on an empty tube or a tube whose top coin matches the colour being moved. This rule is what creates the puzzle complexity. Without it, any sorting order would work. With it, the sequence of moves matters deeply — a move that looks helpful now can block a necessary move three steps later. Advanced Coin Sort players don't just evaluate whether a move is valid; they evaluate whether it's recoverable if the next two or three moves don't go as planned.

howToPlayPage.difficultyProgression: Coin Sort scales difficulty through two primary variables: the number of colours in play and the number of empty tubes available. Early levels (1-20) use three to four colours with two empty tubes, giving players enough space to experiment and recover from mistakes. Mid-range levels (21-60) introduce five colours and reduce empty tubes to one, requiring more deliberate planning. Advanced levels (61-100+) use six colours with minimal empty tube availability, where the solution requires finding a specific move sequence — trial-and-error is no longer viable, and players must reason through the configuration from the starting position.

tips.title: Never Fill Empty Tubes Early
tips.desc: The most common mistake in Coin Sort is using the empty tubes as permanent storage for mid-level moves. Once an empty tube holds a mixed colour arrangement, it functions as just another blocked tube. Protect empty tubes until you specifically need them for the next planned move sequence. They are your most valuable resource — spend them deliberately.

tips.title: Work on One Colour at a Time
tips.desc: Attempting to sort all colours simultaneously spreads your moves across too many partial stacks and usually results in a gridlocked board. Identify the colour with the most coins already on top across tubes and consolidate it fully first. One completed colour tube reduces the problem size and reveals better options for the remaining colours.

tips.title: Plan Three Moves Ahead
tips.desc: In early Coin Sort levels, individual move evaluation is enough. From level 20 onwards, the puzzle requires looking three to four moves ahead before committing. Specifically: after the move you're considering, what moves become available? What moves become blocked? If a move creates a configuration where the next two moves are forced and one of them is a dead end, the original move was wrong.

tips.title: Restart Without Hesitation
tips.desc: Coin Sort levels are fully solvable by design. If you reach a state where no valid moves remain that make progress, the fastest path forward is restarting the level. Restarting is not failure — it's new information. Each restart reveals part of the solution space that trial moves had already explored, which makes the next attempt more informed.

tips.title: Use the Undo Button Strategically
tips.desc: Most Coin Sort implementations include an undo function. Use it specifically for move-and-see evaluation: make a move, assess whether the board state is better or worse, and undo it if the result is unfavourable. This approach turns the undo button into a planning tool rather than a mistake-correction tool. It's the difference between reactive and proactive puzzle-solving.

posts.title: Getting Started with Coin Sort: A Complete Beginner's Guide
posts.excerpt: New to Coin Sort? This guide explains the move rules, how to approach your first levels, and the habits that separate good puzzle-solvers from great ones.

sections.heading: What Is Coin Sort?
paragraphs: Coin Sort is a logic puzzle game where you sort mixed stacks of coloured coins into single-colour tubes. Each tube starts with a random arrangement of two or more colours. Your task is to move coins between tubes until each tube holds only one colour. The constraint: you can only move the top coin from any tube, and you can only place it on an empty tube or one where the top coin already there matches your colour.

The game has no time pressure, no fail states, and no lives. Every level is solvable — the question is finding the correct sequence of moves. Coin Sort rewards methodical thinking over speed. Players who take time to plan before acting consistently solve levels with fewer moves and fewer restarts.

sections.heading: How to Open the Game
paragraphs: Navigate to the Play page on this site. Coin Sort loads directly in your browser — desktop, tablet, and smartphone all work without any download or account. Progress is saved automatically in your browser, so you can close the tab and return to the same level later.

The interface shows all tubes and coins from the first second. Tap any tube to select the top coin, then tap a destination tube to place it. The game highlights valid destination tubes so you always know which moves are available.

sections.heading: Your First Five Minutes
paragraphs: In your first level, before making any move, count how many colours are present and identify which colour has the most coins exposed on top across all tubes. That colour is your starting point — it has the most accessible coins and sorting it first creates the maximum space for subsequent moves.

Work on fully sorting one colour before starting another. Partially sorting multiple colours simultaneously tends to create configurations where no valid progress moves exist. One complete colour tube reduces the active puzzle complexity by a full stack's worth of coins.

sections.heading: Ready to Sort?
paragraphs: Head to the Play page, look at the first puzzle for ten seconds before touching anything, identify the most accessible colour, and sort it completely. That discipline — look before moving — is the single habit that makes the biggest difference in Coin Sort.

posts.title: Top Tips & Tricks for Coin Sort
posts.excerpt: These Coin Sort strategies are what experienced puzzle solvers use to clear levels efficiently and avoid getting stuck.

sections.heading: Protect Your Empty Tubes
paragraphs: Empty tubes are the most valuable resource in Coin Sort. They function as temporary holding positions that allow you to unblock coins buried beneath other colours. The common beginner mistake is filling empty tubes early in a level with whatever coin needs to move next, effectively converting them into blocked tubes.

Discipline around empty tubes means: never place a coin onto an empty tube unless you have a specific plan for how that coin completes a colour sequence within the next three moves. If you can't articulate that plan, use a different move. Protecting empty tubes is the single most impactful technique in advanced Coin Sort levels.

sections.heading: Complete One Colour First
paragraphs: Sorting one colour completely before working on another reduces the active puzzle complexity faster than spreading moves across multiple colours simultaneously. Once a tube holds a complete single-colour stack, remove it from your mental model — it's done. The remaining puzzle is simpler.

To identify which colour to complete first: find the colour that has the most coins accessible from tube tops across the board. More accessible coins means fewer preparatory moves before you can consolidate that colour's full stack.

sections.heading: Read Dead Ends Before They Happen
paragraphs: A dead end in Coin Sort is a board state where no valid move makes progress. Dead ends are always created by a specific earlier decision — usually filling an empty tube with the wrong colour or scattering one colour's coins so widely that none can move without blocking others.

Before each move, ask: does this move create a new inaccessible colour anywhere on the board? If a move buries a colour's last exposed coin under another colour with no valid destination, that move is likely creating a future dead end. Pausing to check this specific condition prevents most restarts.

sections.heading: Use Restarts as Data
paragraphs: Every restart in Coin Sort is a learning event, not a failure. When you restart, you know which specific configuration led to the dead end. The next attempt can avoid that configuration deliberately — try a different move sequence in the first four or five turns and see how it diverges.

Experienced Coin Sort players treat restarts as rapid hypothesis testing. Each attempt either solves the level or eliminates one approach from the solution space. Levels that initially seem unsolvable usually yield within three or four intentional restarts because each attempt narrows the relevant decision points.

posts.title: The Cognitive Benefits of Playing Coin Sort
posts.excerpt: Sorting and sequencing puzzles are among the most cognitively demanding casual game types. Here is what research shows about their benefits.

sections.heading: Sorting Puzzles and the Brain
paragraphs: Sequencing and sorting puzzles engage the prefrontal cortex — specifically the regions responsible for planning, working memory, and inhibitory control. Research on logic puzzle games consistently shows improvements in these executive functions among regular players, with effects observed after sessions as short as twenty minutes.

Coin Sort specifically trains the ability to hold multiple constraint states simultaneously in working memory: which coins are where, which moves are valid, and which future states are accessible from the current one. This multi-state tracking ability is directly analogous to the kind of complex reasoning required in fields like programming, logistics, and strategic planning.

sections.heading: Planning and Problem-Solving
paragraphs: The defining cognitive demand of Coin Sort is move-ahead planning. Advanced levels cannot be solved reactively — they require the player to reason about board states two, three, or four moves ahead and select current moves based on their future consequences rather than their immediate validity.

This type of forward-planning reasoning is one of the most transferable cognitive skills developed through puzzle games. Studies on chess, sliding puzzles, and sorting games all find improvements in planning depth — the number of moves a player can evaluate simultaneously before committing — after regular engagement with move-ahead constraint puzzles.

sections.heading: Stress Relief Through Focused Engagement
paragraphs: Logic puzzles produce a cognitive state researchers call 'focused absorption' — the complete engagement of attention on a problem that excludes environmental distractions and reduces conscious rumination. This state reliably lowers cortisol levels and is associated with the subjective experience of being 'in the zone'.

Coin Sort's pace supports this state particularly well. There's no time pressure, no auditory alarm, and no failure penalty. The puzzle waits for you to think. This low-stress environment allows focused absorption to develop fully — the brain enters problem-solving mode without the sympathetic nervous system activation that pressure-based games produce.

sections.heading: Safe Screen Time
paragraphs: Every move in Coin Sort requires active evaluation: is this move valid, and does it advance the solution? There is no passive state. The constant engagement of logical reasoning makes Coin Sort active rather than passive screen time.

The game contains no in-app purchases, no social pressure mechanics, and no advertising targeting children. Session length is self-determined — the game does not use escalating reward loops to prevent stopping. Players can engage for two minutes or two hours without manipulative design patterns influencing their decision to continue.

posts.title: How to Get Better at Coin Sort
posts.excerpt: Coin Sort improvement comes from developing planning depth, learning to read dead ends, and practising deliberate empty-tube management.

sections.heading: Extend Your Planning Depth
paragraphs: The most direct path to Coin Sort improvement is increasing how many moves ahead you can evaluate before committing. New players evaluate one move at a time — is this move valid? Intermediate players evaluate two: is this move valid, and does it leave the board in a state where the next move I need is also valid? Advanced players evaluate three or four, asking not just about the next move but about the chain of moves that leads to the first completed colour tube.

Develop planning depth deliberately by slowing down: before each move, articulate out loud (or in your head) exactly which moves you plan to make in the next three turns and why. This verbal articulation forces explicit planning rather than intuitive guessing, and the habit transfers quickly into faster in-session reasoning.

sections.heading: Master Empty-Tube Discipline
paragraphs: Every Coin Sort player who reaches advanced levels has had the experience of solving a hard puzzle primarily by learning to preserve empty tubes. The transition from intermediate to advanced play almost always passes through this lesson.

Practice empty-tube discipline by imposing a rule: never place a coin onto an empty tube unless that placement is part of a specific three-move sequence you've already planned. Treating empty tubes as expendable early-level resources instead of strategic assets is the most common ceiling that prevents progression to harder levels.

sections.heading: Recognise Colour Accessibility
paragraphs: Coin Sort improvement requires developing rapid pattern recognition for colour accessibility — the ability to look at a board and immediately assess which colours are most and least accessible for consolidation. Accessible colours have multiple coins exposed on tube tops across the board. Inaccessible colours have all remaining coins buried beneath other colours in every tube.

Train this recognition by pausing at the start of each level and ranking all colours from most to least accessible before making any move. This ranking takes fifteen to thirty seconds and frequently reveals a move sequence that wasn't obvious from a quick scan. The habit of explicit accessibility ranking is what differentiates players who solve levels efficiently from those who solve them through extended trial and error.

sections.heading: Replay Hard Levels Intentionally
paragraphs: When a Coin Sort level defeats you consistently, the fastest path to solving it is intentional replay: each restart, make a different opening move sequence and track which four-move start gives you the most viable board state. This systematic variation is more efficient than repeating failed approaches with minor differences.

Most Coin Sort levels have a specific sequence in the first four to six moves that opens the solution path. Finding this sequence through intentional variation and careful observation of the resulting board states is the core puzzle-solving skill the game is designed to develop. Intentional replay turns frustrating difficulty into a solvable search problem.

posts.title: Coin Sort for Kids: A Parent's Complete Guide
posts.excerpt: A guide for parents on Coin Sort — what the game involves, the educational skills it builds, and why it is safe for children.

sections.heading: Is Coin Sort Safe for Children?
paragraphs: Coin Sort is fully safe for players of all ages. The browser version contains no in-app purchases, no advertising targeting children, no social chat features, and no external links. Children access the game anonymously — no account registration, no email address, and no personal data collection of any kind.

The visual content is entirely age-appropriate: simple geometric tubes and brightly coloured coins. There is no violence, no mature content, and no communication with other players. Coin Sort is appropriate for unsupervised play from early primary school age onwards.

sections.heading: What Will My Child Learn?
paragraphs: Coin Sort builds logical sequencing skills directly. Solving a level requires understanding that current actions have future consequences, and planning a sequence of moves based on that understanding. This cause-and-effect reasoning is a foundational skill for mathematics, science, and computer science education.

The game also builds frustration tolerance and iterative problem-solving habits. Levels that require multiple restarts teach children to treat failure as information rather than defeat. Restarting with a different approach, observing what changes, and applying those observations is the scientific method in practice — and Coin Sort makes it engaging enough that children repeat the cycle voluntarily.

sections.heading: Tips for Healthy Screen Time
paragraphs: Coin Sort has natural session completion points — each level ends definitively when the sort is complete. This structure makes it easy to agree on a session limit of two or three levels, because each level has a clear conclusion that feels earned rather than interrupted.

Consider asking your child to explain their plan before they start each level. 'Which colour are you going to sort first, and why?' is a question that develops explicit planning language and turns a puzzle game session into an exercise in articulating strategic thinking. Children who can explain their reasoning aloud are practising a skill that transfers directly to academic problem-solving contexts.

sections.heading: COPPA Compliance
paragraphs: Coin Sort does not collect personal information from any user, including children under 13. No registration is required, and no user data is stored beyond local browser information that clears automatically.

There are no advertisements, no social features, no external links, and no in-app purchase mechanisms in the browser version. The game operates as a self-contained puzzle experience with no data practices that raise COPPA concerns. It is appropriate for classroom use and unsupervised home play at all ages.
